channel.title: AI Agents on Sujith Quintelier
channel.description: Recent content in AI Agents on Sujith Quintelier

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure MCP Server 3.0
item.description:
Azure MCP Server 3.0 is now generally available. The release expands Azure integration for AI agents and developer tools via the open Model Context Protocol (MCP), including new infrastructure-as-code support through Azure Terraform.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: security: Agents are your newest insiders. Security must move at their speed.
item.description:
Microsoft announced new capabilities in Microsoft 365 E7 and Project Perception aimed at helping organizations contain AI agent risk and continuously adapt protection. The post frames agents as insider-like risks and focuses on security controls that keep pace with their behavior.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: commandline: Copilot to autopilot: Why no single safeguard is enough
item.description:
Microsoft says it built a layered control model for an AI agent to handle production network incidents autonomously, but only within defined identity, authorization, tooling, and human-approval boundaries. The article argues that no single safeguard is sufficient for production use.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: dotnet: Durable Task in the Real World: What Problems Does It Actually Solve?
item.description:
The post outlines practical cases where durable execution is useful, where it is unnecessary, and how it relates to AI agents. It frames Durable Task as a tool for workflows that need reliable state, retries, and long-running coordination.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Microsoft SQL Agent Skills
item.description:
Microsoft SQL Agent Skills are in public preview. They provide product-specific guidance for AI agents used to build, operate, and migrate SQL workloads across Azure SQL Database, Azure SQL Database container, and SQL Server migration scenarios.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: security: ​​​​​​​​What’s new in Microsoft Security: September 2026​​
item.description:
Microsoft Security’s September 2026 update focuses on discovering and controlling local AI agents, extending Zero Trust controls to agent traffic, and improving SOC foundational capabilities.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Foundry Routines in Foundry Agent Service
item.description:
Foundry Agent Service now includes Foundry Routines in public preview. This adds a native trigger primitive so published agents can run automatically on schedules or in response to business events.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: dotnet: Build Your Own AI Agent Harness in C#, the MafClaw Live Series
item.description:
Microsoft is running a 4-part live series showing how to build a C# AI agent harness with Microsoft Agent Framework, starting from a single IChatClient call and evolving it into a production-ready agent with observability and governance. The post is an announcement for the series and does not include technical implementation details.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: commandline: Who spent all the tokens? Real-time, run-scoped cost control for AI agents
item.description:
TokenOps is presented as a run-scoped cost control mechanism for AI agents that enforces a shared budget in real time. The stated goal is to stop runaway runs before costs accumulate and invoices arrive.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Markdown for Agents in Azure App Service
item.description:
Azure App Service now has a public preview of Markdown for Agents. When a client requests Markdown, App Service can automatically serve a cleaner Markdown version of app content for AI agents and other tools.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: commandline: 🌿 Agent Terrarium: Bringing AI agents to life
item.description:
A weekend open-source desktop companion app, Agent Terrarium, explores a more interactive, less purely transactional way to work with AI agents.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: security: Advance Zero Trust for AI: New tools and guidance to secure AI agents and DevSecOps
item.description:
Microsoft says it is expanding its Zero Trust for AI strategy with new tools and guidance aimed at securing AI agents and DevSecOps environments. The post highlights a broader security approach for AI and related development workflows.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog
